note: FIVE BACKLOG CARDS, FOUR SHIPPED AND ONE STOPPED. (1+2) THE-110 AND THE-127 ARE ONE ROOT CAUSE: a capability gate answers THREE things - permitted, not permitted, and NOT YET KNOWN - and every gate collapsed the third into one of the other two. AdminBlog's `canAutomate` was `tenantPlan ? getPlanFeatures(tenantPlan).automatedBlog : false`, so a plan that had not loaded read as a REFUSAL: the Automate button was absent on first paint, appeared when the tenant document resolved, and blinked whenever THE-259's bounded re-read republished the tier. `usePlanGate` collapses it the other way (`if (!ctx.tenantPlan) return true`), which flashes a control the church may not have and then retracts it. `utils/plan-gate-state.ts` returns the third state instead of picking a wrong one, and the header renders it as a `skeleton` IN THE CONTROL'S OWN FOOTPRINT - neither wrong answer, and no reflow when the answer lands, which was the other half of the flicker. FAIL-CLOSED APPLIES TO CAPS AND NOT TO CAPABILITY GATES, and the type signature enforces that rather than a reviewer noticing: `resolvePlanGateState` takes a `BooleanFeatureCell` derived from `PlanFeatures`, so a numeric cap cannot be passed in. A cap protects Harvest (over-granting creates a resource nobody bought and nothing reconciles it); a capability gate protects nobody, because card 86bbtx3dj settled that plan caps are client-side by design and firestore.rules scopes by membership and permission, never by plan. `maxCourses`'s deliberate fall-back to `plus` on an unknown plan is UNTOUCHED and pinned by a no-regression test. THE-127'S PREMISE IS CORRECTED RATHER THAN ADOPTED: the card says a church in grace is briefly told it cannot do something it can, and that does not follow. `recordDodoSubscriptionOnHold` writes ONE timestamp to the server-only private document and explicitly leaves `tenants/{id}.status` on `active` - "the church keeps giving, publishing and sending for the whole window" - so a church inside grace is permitted everything by the recorded status alone and the client gate needs no sight of grace to get that right. `tenantAllows(undefined)` already fails OPEN too. What the gates were actually exposed to is the PLAN, which is what was fixed. (3) THE-108 IS STOPPED, and the stop is evidenced with the compiler rather than argued. The forked and canonical Course types are not assignable in EITHER direction: fork to canonical fails TS2322 (`id` is `string | undefined` against `string`), canonical to fork fails TS2741 (`status` is missing but required). The forked Lesson requires six fields the canonical one marks optional - youtubeUrl, outline, sources, scripture, quiz, teacherNote - all read unconditionally by the editor. The fork carries four fields the canonical Course does not: status, author, coverImage, createdAt. The canonical file ALREADY RECORDS THE SPLIT AS DELIBERATE. Unifying is a change to a type 17 non-test modules import and that LibraryCourse extends, not an edit to one component. The drift is PINNED field by field off a real parse so the finding cannot evaporate. THE-345's countedAdoptions/adoptedResolvedKey/danglingAdoptions and THE-342's readDocsByIds all live in AdminCourses.tsx, not the editor, and are asserted unchanged. (4) THE-141: the header read the WRONG FIELD. `users/{uid}.photoURL` is Firestore and is what an upload writes; `auth.currentUser.photoURL` is the Auth profile and is what a provider writes. Six surfaces read the Firestore one; the header alone read the Auth one, via the store's `currentUser`. Google members looked fine (the provider fills the Auth profile), which is why it read as intermittent; an email/password member's upload is a data URI that Firebase Auth will not hold, so `updateProfile` rejects, the Firestore write lands, and the header showed a letter. THE `ui/avatar` ADOPTION IS SPLIT OUT AND REPORTED: it is presentation the defect does not need and it moves this header's tags, class literals, colour tokens and rendered-row inventory - six assertions across three frozen baselines - so the FIELD changed and the markup did not. A FAILED READ SURFACES through `handleFirestoreError` rather than being indistinguishable from "no photo", and the letter avatar remains the fallback. (5) THE-104: THE CRON DOES NOT FAIL, ESTABLISHED FROM PRODUCTION. Vercel runtime logs for project harvest-agent, branch main: `GET /api/blog/auto-generate 200`. Sentry org harvest-jf over fourteen days: ten error events across two signatures, none blog-related and none carrying a blog-auto-generate step. The retry-loop work fixed it. BUT ONE EXIT COULD STILL VANISH and that is the real finding: the route's per-tenant failure reaches Sentry AND the settings document AdminBlog renders, and its whole-run failure reaches Sentry AND returns 500, while its AUTH REFUSAL returned 401 with NO capture and NO log. A CRON_SECRET never set, or rotated on one side, is then a daily 401 that reaches no error tracker: the feature stops posting for every tenant and the only trace is a status code nobody reads. It now reports to Sentry with a distinct reason and names that reason in the response. THE CRON SHOULD KEEP RUNNING: `automatedBlog` is Ministry-only and is READ by a real server-side gate in this very route, recorded in docs/plan-features-flag-audit.md - not one of the phantom cells that were deleted for naming capabilities nobody built. NO NEW DEPENDENCY, TOKEN OR PRIMITIVE was installed. THE-363 RECORDS NO firestore.rules DIGEST ANYWHERE: it adds no Firestore operation, and its rules assertion is a CONTENT claim (the rules still scope by membership and permission, and read no tier) rather than a digest literal - the mistake this register caught #504 making. Every guard was verified by MUTATION - collapse unknown into denied, collapse it into permitted, loosen the course cap, unify a forked field in each direction, read the Auth photo again, delete the letter fallback, make the cron 401 silent, plant a line-number pin, plant a branch-diff guard, plant an emoji - and every one failed before being restored. TWO OF THIS TICKET'S OWN GUARDS COULD NOT FAIL ON FIRST WRITE and were found by mutation, not by reading: the cron's structural exit check matched the IMPORT of `captureHandledError` rather than a call, and the frozen-path check spelled the root layout filename whole in its own `it(...)` title and failure message, so the file matched itself.

entries.why: THE-363 OWNS the automation GATE in this file and one pre-existing emoji, and nothing else in it. (1) THE GATE. `canAutomate` was `hasPlatformOverride() || (tenantPlan ? getPlanFeatures(tenantPlan).automatedBlog : false)` - three states collapsed into two, with NOT-YET-KNOWN falling into NOT PERMITTED. It now resolves through `resolvePlanGateState('automatedBlog', { plan, platformOverride })` to a named 'permitted' | 'denied' | 'unknown', and the header renders all three: the control when permitted, NOTHING when denied, and a `skeleton` sized to the control's own footprint when unknown. The `useEffect` that loads automation settings still keys off a BOOLEAN (`planGatePermits`), because a fetch fired on an unresolved entitlement asks for something nobody has established the church can have - so the side effect is unchanged in behaviour while the RENDER gained a third branch. The import of `getPlanFeatures` is replaced by the gate module; no other call site in this file read it. (2) THE EMOJI. The Generate Now button's label carried U+26A1, which THE-347 RECORDED rather than removed and named as "pre-existing work and its own ticket". This is that ticket: the glyph is gone, replaced by the `Sparkles` lucide icon already imported and already used by the Automate control beside it, so the button says the same thing without shipping an emoji. THE-347's RECORDED_EMOJI entry for this file goes from [U+26A1] to [] - a TIGHTENING, not a loosening: a first emoji in this file now fails where a second used to. Both touched buttons gained an explicit `min-h-[44px]`, which neither had. NO READ, NO WRITE AND NO ENDPOINT MOVED: the `blog_posts` listener, its tenant scoping, `sortByTime`, the `/api/blog/automate` GET and POST, `handleGenerateNow`, `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES` and the whole failure panel are byte-identical. THE-347's `formatFirestoreDate` call and its FirestoreDate interface are untouched and its guards still measure them.

THE-363 owns ONE EXPRESSION in the desktop header and nothing else in this file. The profile control read `currentUser?.photoURL`, where `currentUser` is the Firebase AUTH user the store holds from `onAuthStateChanged` - so it showed the photo the IDENTITY PROVIDER supplied and never the one the member UPLOADED. Profile.tsx, PersonalInformationModal.tsx, AdminCRM, AdminCommunity's MessageAvatar, UserMessages and NewsTab all read `users/{uid}.photoURL` from Firestore; this header was the only surface asking a different question. It now reads `useMemberPhoto()`, which subscribes to the member's own user document and falls back to the Auth profile - both kept, because the Auth value is what makes a Google member's photo correct on the FIRST paint while the document is still in flight. THE ELEMENT TREE, EVERY CLASS LITERAL, EVERY COLOUR TOKEN AND THE RENDERED ROW INVENTORY ARE UNCHANGED, and that is deliberate and load-bearing rather than incidental. Adopting `ui/avatar` here - which the brief asked for - replaces one img and one span with three primitive elements and moves all four inventories, which is six assertions across MemberScreens.desktop-layout, THE-295 and THE-348, each needing its own reversible fold and meta-guard. That is a PRESENTATION change the defect does not require, `main` went red for everyone once because a PR replaced a pinned baseline, and this ticket's brief says to split out anything that turns out large. So it is SPLIT AND REPORTED: same markup, same classes, different FIELD. The only additions are the import, the hook call, a `data-testid` on the control so the guard can find it without a line number, and a comment - and the comment is written with NO house emoji and with no angle-bracket tag names in its prose, because THE-295 censuses this file's emoji exactly and counts tags over UNSTRIPPED source, and the first draft of it turned both of those red. THE-348's `isChatOpen` nav condition and content-wrapper template, THE-362's `onDonate` jump to the partner tab, THE-295's `pb-[calc(8px+env(safe-area-inset-bottom))]`, every tab gate, `hasGiving`, `hasGivingRails` and the whole nav derivation are byte-identical.
